    AI Overview
    To file a federal tax extension and get until October 15 to file, submit Form 4868 by April 15. You can do this for free via IRS Free File, using tax software, or by paying all/part of your taxes owed online IRS Direct Pay and selecting "Extension". Note that an extension is to file, not to pay taxes owed. 
    Top Ways to File a Tax Extension 
    • IRS Free File (Recommended): Use IRS Free File to electronically submit Form 4868 for free, regardless of income.
    • Electronic Payment: Make a partial or full payment via IRS Direct Pay, debit/credit card, or Digital Wallet, and select "4868" or "Extension" as the reason. This automatically triggers an extension without filing the form separately.
    • Tax Software/Pro:
      Use tax software (e.g., TurboTax, H&R Block) or a tax professional to e-file.
    • Mail: File a paper Form 4868 by mail. It must be postmarked by April 15. 
    Important Considerations 
    • Deadline: The extension request must be submitted by April 15.
    • Payment Requirement: If you owe taxes, you must still pay the estimated amount due by April 15 to avoid penalties and interest.
    • Eligibility: Anyone can file an extension, regardless of income.
    • Confirmation: E-filing provides a confirmation number for your records.
    • State Taxes: A federal extension does not always cover state taxes; check your state's tax agency requirements.

    What is the easiest way to file a tax extension?
    An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
    AI Overview
    The easiest way to file a tax extension is by paying all or part of your estimated tax owed using IRS Direct Pay, a credit/debit card, or the Electronic Federal Tax Payment System (EFTPS) and selecting "Extension" as the reason. This method eliminates the need to file Form 4868 separately. 
    Top Ways to File an Extension (by April 15): 
    • Fastest/Easiest (If Owe Money): Use IRS Direct Pay. Select "Extension" as the payment type, and you will receive a confirmation number, automatically granting a 6-month extension to file.
    • Free E-Filing (No Payment Needed): Use IRS Free File to submit Form 4868 electronically, available to all filers.
    • Tax Software: Use software like H&R Block or TurboTax to submit an electronic extension. 
    Crucial Tips: 
    • Extension to File, Not Pay: An extension gives you until October 15 to file, but you must pay any estimated taxes owed by April 15 to avoid penalties.
    • Deadline: You must file the extension request by April 15th.
    • Mail Option: You can mail Form 4868, but it must be postmarked by April 15. 
    Disclaimer: This information is for the 2024/2025 tax year. Always check IRS.gov for the most current deadlines.

      Dec 22, 2025 — A tax return extension gives you six more months to file, but you must still pay your taxes on time. Learn about tax return extensions or how to pay your tax ...Read more
      How to file for a tax extension

      While you will get more time to file your return, an extension does not grant you more time to pay your taxes. To avoid possible penalties, you should estimate and pay your federal taxes by the due date.

      Learn the ways to request an extension:
      • Online using IRS Free File
      • When you pay your estimated tax bill
      • Using IRS Form 4868
      How to pay taxes in installments

      If you feel that you may not be able to pay your tax bill in full by the due date, you may be eligible to pay in installments. Learn more about the IRS' payment plans and what additional costs and fees you may have to pay.
